summary: Repaired /srv/inventory on node1 and verified persistence after reboot. Existing data was preserved; RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created system group inventory-readers and system account inventorysvc using existing OS tools.
Set all inventory entries to inventorysvc:inventory-readers.
Set directories to 750 and regular files to 640, removing all permissions for other users.
Verified group-reader access succeeds and unrelated-user access is denied.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified a changed boot ID, healthy system state, identities, permissions, access controls, and data hashes.

evidence.summary: The two files retained identical SHA-256 hashes before changes, after changes, and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Data owned by inventorysvc and readable by inventory-readers
evidence.summary: All entries are inventorysvc:inventory-readers; directories are 750, files are 640, and effective group-reader access succeeds.
No entry has other-user permission bits, and direct unrelated-user read attempts were denied before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel preserved
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 were unchanged across the repair and reboot.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 6ab6a71b-188c-48ae-971b-a6bb378b1d72, acknowledged the safe reboot, observed new boot ID 6d62da6f-9f41-48c3-abca-4ec83afcdd81, and verified running system state plus recovered data and access controls.
